rubric.task_read: Implement AlphaFold-3 outgoing TriMul as a Triton kernel that is correct across a large domain (3 batch × 8 seqlens × 4 dims, masked/unmasked, Normal and heavy-tailed Cauchy inputs, within 2e-2 tolerance) and fast enough (max-of-10 medians ≤10400μs on H100). Long-horizon and complex: the spec hides many subtle correctness traps (outgoing vs incoming contraction, LayerNorm/gate/linear ordering, where the mask applies, single shared norm feeding five projections) and demands numerical robustness plus multi-shape performance tuning. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in precise spec reading, building an independent reference oracle, staged correctness-then-latency milestones, and disciplined verification across the whole domain.

dimensions.name: Spec decoding & environment probing
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact TriMul math from a prose spec littered with ordering/placement traps, and probing the Triton/GPU environment before committing to a kernel design.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec encodes at least five silent correctness traps (outgoing contraction = left@right.T over the inner axis, single shared LayerNorm feeding all five projections, mask applied only at the projection*gate step, LN_hidden then out_gate before to_out, nomask semantics). Misreading any one produces a plausible-looking kernel that is wrong everywhere. Orientation is the difference between building the right thing and debugging the wrong thing for hours.

anchors.0: Starts coding a kernel with no evidence of parsing the contraction direction, norm/gate ordering, or mask placement; treats it as generic 'matmul + norm'.
anchors.3: Reads the spec once and captures the obvious structure but leaves at least one trap unresolved (e.g. uses left@right instead of left@right.T, or applies mask in the wrong place) without noticing.
anchors.5: Correctly identifies all the major spec details (outgoing contraction, shared norm, mask location, gate-before-to_out) and confirms hidden_dim=128, dtype float32, and the shape contract before building.
anchors.8: Systematically enumerates every ordering/placement trap and cross-checks each against the einsum and prose independently; probes Triton availability, autotune constraints, and the numeric implications of Cauchy γ=2 heavy tails against a 2e-2 tolerance before designing the kernel.
anchors.10: Above, plus derives a precise mental/written model of the whole data flow (dims of each intermediate, why the contraction is over k, how nomask degenerates) and anticipates where float32 accumulation over large N and heavy-tailed inputs threatens the tolerance — turning spec reading into concrete design constraints.

dimensions.name: Correctness-first staging
dimensions.description: Breaking the build into ordered milestones — reference oracle, a correct-but-slow kernel, then latency optimization — each with an explicit done-check, rather than one monolithic push at a fused fast kernel.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task explicitly prioritizes correctness over latency across a huge domain, then adds a hard latency gate. Jumping straight to a fused, autotuned kernel makes correctness bugs and performance bugs indistinguishable. Clean staging (get it provably right, then make it fast) is what keeps this tractable over the horizon.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated attempt at a fast fused kernel; no separation of correctness from performance, no sub-goals.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering (roughly does correctness before speed) but no explicit milestones or done-criteria; correctness and optimization changes interleave chaotically.
anchors.5: Explicit stages: build/borrow a reference, get a straightforward kernel matching it on a few shapes, then optimize — each with a rough success check.
anchors.8: Milestones are ordered and each has a concrete exit test (reference matches PyTorch TriMul; naive kernel matches reference across the full shape/dtype/mask grid; only then tune latency against the 10 timed shapes), so a regression at any stage is localized.
anchors.10: Above, with milestones sequenced by risk (nail the contraction and numerics on the hardest Cauchy/large-N cases first, treat performance as a separate track gated on a frozen correct baseline), and the optimization stage itself decomposed (per-shape tiling/blocking) with per-milestone checks that prevent fast-but-wrong regressions.

dimensions.name: Building a correctness oracle & domain sweep
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing an independent ground-truth (a clean PyTorch TriMul) and sweeping the kernel against it across shapes, dtypes, mask/nomask, and Normal/Cauchy inputs — not just eyeballing one shape.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader checks correctness across ~192 domain combinations within 2e-2, including heavy-tailed inputs that stress numerical stability. Without a self-built oracle and a systematic sweep, an agent cannot know it is correct — success on one shape says almost nothing about N=2048 or Cauchy γ=2. This is the single highest-leverage meta-work faculty here.

anchors.0: No independent reference; correctness asserted from the kernel running without error or matching a single hand-picked case.
anchors.3: Compares against a reference on one or two easy shapes only; no coverage of large N, dim variety, mask/nomask, or Cauchy inputs.
anchors.5: Builds a correct PyTorch reference and checks the kernel against it on a representative spread of shapes and at least one masked and one Cauchy case, using the stated tolerance.
anchors.8: Constructs a trustworthy reference and a systematic parametrized sweep covering the batch×N×dim grid, both mask states, and both distributions with rtol=atol=2e-2; treats any mismatch as a blocking failure and localizes it.
anchors.10: Above, plus verifies the reference itself against the spec's einsum, stresses the numerically hardest corners deliberately (largest N with Cauchy γ=2 to probe accumulation error), and separates 'is the math right' from 'is the tolerance met' — designing checks that would catch subtle contraction/ordering errors that pass on small inputs but fail at scale.

dimensions.name: Tracking correctness & latency across the domain
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which shapes/distributions pass and which of the 10 timed shapes meet the latency budget, and detecting when fixes for one case break another.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~192 correctness combinations and 10 latency targets scored by the worst-case median, progress is multi-dimensional. An agent that loses track — fixing Cauchy stability while silently regressing a large-N shape, or optimizing one shape past budget while another blows up — will thrash. Keeping an honest done-vs-remaining ledger is essential over this horizon.

anchors.0: No sense of overall status; declares done after a single passing run with no view of remaining shapes or the latency worst case.
anchors.3: Tracks progress vaguely ('seems to work now') without per-shape/per-distribution status or latency-per-shape awareness.
anchors.5: Keeps a clear running account of which cases pass correctness and roughly where latency stands against the 10-shape max, and notices obvious regressions.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit ledger of correctness across the grid and per-shape latency vs the 10400μs gate, identifies the binding worst-case shape, and catches cross-case regressions when a change helps one shape and hurts another.
anchors.10: Above, with early detection of stuck/circular states (e.g. repeatedly re-tuning a shape that is not the bottleneck, or oscillating between two failing corners) and reallocation of effort toward whatever actually gates the score — sustained, accurate situational awareness across both correctness and latency axes.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on numeric & performance failures
dimensions.description: Revising the kernel design when reality diverges — a contraction/ordering bug surfaces, Cauchy inputs violate tolerance, or a shape misses the latency budget — instead of pushing harder on a falsified approach.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Heavy-tailed inputs, large-N accumulation, and a strict worst-case latency gate almost guarantee that the first design will fail somewhere. The decisive skill is diagnosing the true cause (wrong axis vs numeric overflow vs bad tiling) and changing the design accordingly, rather than tweaking constants in circles.

anchors.0: Ignores failures or repeats the same failing approach; no diagnosis when a shape is wrong or slow.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with blind tweaks (nudging tolerances, retrying autotune) without isolating the cause.
anchors.5: When a case fails, forms a hypothesis about why (e.g. mask placement, accumulation precision, block size) and makes a targeted fix that resolves it.
anchors.8: Distinguishes correctness failures from performance failures and root-causes each — e.g. tracing a Cauchy tolerance miss to accumulation strategy, or a slow shape to tiling — then revises the design deliberately and re-verifies without regressing prior wins.
anchors.10: Demonstrates sustained, evidence-driven correction across multiple distinct failures (numeric stability, a wrong intermediate, a bottleneck shape), sometimes revisiting earlier design decisions, and knows when to stop optimizing a shape that already clears the gate — adapting the plan itself, not just the code.
